sections.label: SICC jurisdiction and procedure changes
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies the SICC's jurisdiction over international commercial arbitration proceedings and removes pre-action certification.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, the Bill makes clear that the SICC has jurisdiction to hear any proceedings relating to international commercial arbitration that the High Court may hear under the International Arbitration Act (IAA).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill streamlines the SICC's procedure by removing the option of pre-action certification.

sections.label: SICC cases heard since establishment
sections.summary: The SICC has heard 17 cases with diverse subject matters and parties from various jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since its establishment, the SICC has heard 17 cases with diverse subject matters, including construction, investment, banking and finance and shipbuilding, and involving parties from jurisdictions including Japan, Israel, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Hong Kong, India, Indonesia and Australia.

sections.label: Singapore lawyers for IAA matters
sections.summary: Parties in SICC arbitration-related matters must be represented by Singapore-qualified lawyers, and the Rules of Court will be amended accordingly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The IAA is part of Singapore law, with features that are tailored for the Singapore arbitration landscape, and there is a developed body of local jurisprudence based on our Courts' interpretation and application of the IAA provisions, which Singapore lawyers are well versed in.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, parties which have arbitration-related matters heard in the SICC must be represented by Singapore-qualified lawyers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Foreign lawyers, who may be registered to represent parties in an "offshore case" as defined in the Rules of Court, will not be able to appear before the SICC in respect of IAA matters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Rules of Court will be amended accordingly to clarify that an "offshore case" does not include matters under the IAA.

sections.label: Bill amends Act for SICC jurisdiction
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Act to clarify that the SICC has jurisdiction to hear international commercial arbitration proceedings that the High Court may hear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Leveraging on our existing well-developed legal infrastructure and respected judiciary, which includes not just local judges but eminent jurists drawn from outside Singapore, the establishment of the SICC heralded an exciting change in our legal landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to amend the Act to clarify that the SICC has the jurisdiction to hear any proceedings relating to international commercial arbitration that the High Court may hear.

sections.label: Question on pre-action certificate abolishment
sections.summary: A question is asked about what changed to make the pre-action certificate procedure no longer needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Next, on the issue of the abolishment of the pre-action certificate procedure, during the Second Reading of the Amendment Bill to establish the SICC in late-2014, the hon Law Minister explained that this was an optional step that a party could take in advance of commencing actual proceedings in order to mitigate any uncertainty in whether the dispute falls within the jurisdiction of the SICC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Now that that the SICC has had a few years of experience in administering international commercial disputes heard in that Court, may I ask what has changed that has led to a determination that the pre-action certificate procedure is no longer needed?

sections.label: Offshore case contentions raised early
sections.summary: Contentions on whether a case is an offshore case should be raised and disposed of at the outset.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To promote greater certainty, it is preferable for any contentions as to whether the case is an offshore case to be raised and disposed of at the outset, either before the action is commenced or before the action is materially progressed.

sections.label: SICC dispute resolution hub
sections.summary: Amendments to the Supreme Court of Judicature (Amendment) Bill clarify that the SICC has jurisdiction over all international commercial arbitration matters.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SICC has proven that it is able to quickly resolve complex disputes of substantial value and, together with the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC), and the Singapore International Mediation Centre, is an important component of Singapore's standing as a leading dispute resolution hub of choice in Asia.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is thus only fitting, Mr Deputy Speaker, that on the third year anniversary since its launch, amendments have been proposed to the Supreme Court of Judicature (Amendment) Bill to clarify that the SICC has jurisdiction over all international commercial arbitration matters.

sections.label: Hague Convention and investor-state arbitration
sections.summary: Questions ask whether ratification of the Hague Convention helped enforcement and whether amendments clarify SICC supervision of investor-state arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More specifically, has Singapore's ratification of the Hague Convention on Choice of Court Agreements in 2016, and the passage of enabling legislation by this House just last year, had a positive impact on the enforcement of the Singapore High Court Judgments in general and SICC's judgments in particular?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition to typical commercial arbitration cases which are between two commercial parties, do the amendments also clarify that the SICC can sit, if certain conditions are met, as the supervisory Court in investor-state arbitration cases as well under the International Arbitration Act, particularly section 10 of the International Arbitration Act?

sections.label: Removal of pre-action certificate
sections.summary: A question asks the Senior Minister of State to confirm the rationale for removing the pre-action certificate and any alternative procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Similar to the point that Mr Murali Pillai had made, I would like to ask if the Senior Minister of State can confirm the rationale for removing the pre-action certificate and also whether there will be alternative procedures in place available to parties to now obtain early determination of these jurisdictional issues.

sections.label: Need for amendment questioned
sections.summary: A question asks why the amendment is needed given the International Arbitration Act and section 18 already provide recourse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that such recourse to the High Court is already provided for in the International Arbitration Act and section 18 of the Act already provides that the SICC has jurisdiction where the High Court has jurisdiction, why is there a need for this amendment?

sections.label: Clarifying existing SICC jurisdiction
sections.summary: A question asks whether the amendment only clarifies the jurisdiction the SICC already has rather than conferring additional jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can it be clarified that this amendment does not seek to confer additional jurisdiction but simply to clarify the jurisdiction that the SICC already has?

sections.label: Clarifying section 18D wording
sections.summary: The wording of section 18D is clarified to avoid lingering doubt and unnecessary litigation, without conferring additional jurisdiction on the SICC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With respect to the wording of section 18D of the Supreme Court of Judicature (Amendment) Bill, although we have felt that it was clear, from time to time, we do get some questions as to the wording and its extent, and really, we felt that rather than have any lingering doubt about this, it would be better to clarify it and make it clear from the outset to avoid unnecessary litigation on this going forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And so, to reassure Mr Louis Ng, we are not extending or conferring additional jurisdiction on the SICC.

sections.label: SICC hearing IAA cases
sections.summary: The amendments intend for the SICC to hear IAA-related cases the High Court can hear, subject to jurisdictional requirements and conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The intent of these amendments is for the SICC to hear IAA-related cases that the High Court can hear, subject to the proceedings fulfilling the relevant jurisdictional requirements and conditions.

sections.label: Rules of Court and SICC jurisdiction
sections.summary: The Rules of Court, as subsidiary legislation, cannot enlarge the SICC's jurisdiction under the SCJA, only define or refine it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Whatever the eventual shape and form of the definitions and conditions, the Rules of Court, being subsidiary legislation, cannot enlarge the jurisdiction of the SICC as provided for in the SCJA, they can only serve to define or refine it.

sections.label: Uncertainty over IAA jurisdiction
sections.summary: Uncertainty over SICC jurisdiction to hear IAA matters may explain why it has yet to hear arbitration-related matters, now clarified.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: One possibility why the SICC has yet to hear arbitration-related matters could be precisely the uncertainty over whether the SICC has jurisdiction to hear IAA matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, we have clarified that and we expect that with these amendments, the users will find Singapore an even more attractive seat for arbitration.

sections.label: SICC refining services and suggestions
sections.summary: The SICC will continue to refine and improve its services, and welcomes Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan's suggestions, including converting money judgments to arbitral awards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The SICC will also continue to refine and improve its services to continue to meet the needs of users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And in that respect, I welcome Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan's various suggestions, including the one on the possible "conversion" of money judgments to arbitral awards.
